problem: score_area_for_finding (src/output/json/helpers.rs:209) bucketed a finding into "Forms" via a raw `key.contains("form")` substring check, so any finding whose free-text description contains the word "conformance" (e.g. the contrast rule's "... (supplementary, not a conformance gate)" evidence note) was misrouted into "Forms" with a fabricated "main driver", even though it has nothing to do with form fields.
evidence: Confirmed live in 2 of 5 same-day single-report JSONs generated 2026-08-31: shop.satower-mosterei.de and säfte.com (xn--sfte-loa-com) both showed summary.accessibility_score_breakdown[] area="Forms" with main_driver="Insufficient color contrast (N occurrences)" — root-caused to the contrast rule's evidence message (src/wcag/rules/contrast.rs build_violation) containing "... not a conformance gate.", and "conformance" containing the substring "form" mid-word. Originally also flagged by the report-critic skill's dry-run eval against reports/casoon-batch-en301549.json.
expected: "form" (and the other short keyword checks in score_area_for_finding) should only match at the start of a word, not as a substring anywhere inside an unrelated word. Structurally superseded 2026-09-19 (plan 38): score area classification no longer reads the finding's prose at all. score_area_for_finding now looks the area up in taxonomy::score_area::RULE_AREAS, a total explicit rule_id -> area table, and the text-matching helpers key_has_word_starting_with / strip_css_selector_spans were deleted. This whole bug class can no longer occur; the inventory test every_accessibility_rule_has_a_score_area keeps the table total.
counter_examples: A finding whose rule_id is genuinely forms-related (e.g. a11y.form_labels.missing, whose title/description contain "form"/"Formularfeld" as the start of a word) must still classify into "Forms" once the fix lands.

The pre-existing "Querformat" (German for landscape orientation) case must still not classify as "Forms" — it never starts with "form" as a word, so word-boundary matching also handles it without the earlier hand-written "!contains(format)" exclusion needing to catch it.
